history.new: Exhaustive only for orders <= 15 inside the submonoid of connected graphs (factors with <= 7 vertices); the mechanism that breaks uniqueness for connected graphs under xor (absorption of switching by K2, Theorem 7) is unavailable because 2K1 is disconnected, which explains but does not prove the observation. The Skeptic's own census finds no collision for 141 on connected graphs at any order <= 15.

statement:
Every connected graph has exactly one factorisation into connected primes with respect to the product
(g,h) ~ (g',h') iff (EA, AE, AA or NN); equivalently every graph with connected complement factors uniquely
under the symmetric-difference product into primes with connected complement.
title: Code 141 (EA AE AA NN) has unique factorisation on connected graphs (equivalently, symmetric difference on co-connected graphs)
